raw_text:
Below is a 12-week upper-body–focused program designed for a recreational climber with a history of right subacromial impingement, cleared for pain-free range only and no overhead loading. The plan prioritizes scapular control, rotator cuff capacity, horizontal pulling strength, balanced pushing, and progressive return to climbing-specific demands without provoking symptoms. It also integrates postural work to offset office posture. Full gym assumed.

Key guardrails
- Pain-free range only. Stop any set if pain exceeds 2–3/10 or alters movement.
- No overhead loading. Keep arm positions below shoulder height or within a tolerated scapular plane; no vertical presses, snatches, kipping, etc.
- Tempo focus for control: generally 2–3 seconds eccentric, 1–2 seconds pause where noted, smooth concentric.
- Intensity: leave 2–3 reps in reserve (RIR) on all primary lifts; 1–2 RIR for accessories as tolerated.
- Climbing: limit to easy terrain within pain-free range; avoid dynamic moves, lock-offs near end range, and any overhead aggravation.

Structure overview
- Frequency: 3 upper-focused sessions/week + 1–2 optional low-intensity lower/core/posture sessions.
- Phases (3 x 4 weeks):
  • Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Restore scapular mechanics, isometric/short-range RC strength, gentle horizontal pulling/pressing, tissue capacity.
  • Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progress load via range, leverage, and tempo; introduce stable closed-chain progressions; increase pulling bias.
  • Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength-endurance and climbing-specific capacity; controlled return to low-angle climbing drills; integrate unilateral loading and anti-rotation.

Warm-up template for all sessions (10–12 minutes)
- Breath and ribcage: 90/90 supine breathing with pelvic tilt, 5 breaths.
- T-spine mobility: open-books or quadruped rotations, 6–8/side.
- Scapular activation: scapular push-up plus, 2 x 8–10 pain-free; band W to Y scapular plane partials (stay below 90°), 2 x 10.
- RC priming: sidelying ER (towel under arm), 2 x 12 light; or banded ER at 0–30° abduction, 2 x 12.
- Light blood flow: arm bike 3–4 min easy.

Phase 1: Reposition, control, capacity (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: Pain-free volume, scapular upward/downward rotation control in safe ranges, RC endurance, restore pushing without provocation, build horizontal pull bias (2:1 pull:push).

Week 1
Session A
- Cable row (neutral grip), chest-supported if available: 3 x 12, 3-1-2 tempo.
- Incline push-up on rack (hands well below shoulder line, narrow-neutral grip): 3 x 8–10.
- Sidelying external rotation with 2–4 kg DB: 3 x 12–15.
- Scapular plane DB raise (30–60° only), thumbs up: 2 x 12 light.
- Prone Y (partial to 60°, arms externally rotated), 2 x 10 very light.
- Farmer carry (suitcase carry each side), light–moderate: 3 x 30–40 m/side.

Session B
- Chest-supported rear delt fly (palms down): 3 x 12–15.
- 1-arm cable row (split stance), neutral grip: 3 x 10/side.
- Push-up plus on knees or wall: 3 x 10–12 focusing scapular protraction.
- Banded internal rotation at 0° abduction: 3 x 12–15.
- Low-angle face pull to upper chest (elbows below shoulder height): 3 x 12.
- Pallof press hold: 3 x 20–30 s/side.

Session C
- Landmine press (if tolerated) in scapular plane, partial ROM to pain-free height; else high-incline chest press (30°) with neutral grip: 3 x 8–10 light.
- Chest-supported neutral-grip lat pulldown to chest, elbows stay below or at shoulder height: 3 x 10–12 light–moderate.
- TRX row (high straps, shallow angle): 3 x 10.
- Isometric mid-range ER: 3 x 20–30 s at pain-free effort.
- Biceps cable curl (neutral grip): 2 x 12–15.
- Wrist extensors eccentrics (for climber elbow hygiene): 2 x 12/side.

Week 2
- Progress each exercise by 1–2 reps or small load increase maintaining pain-free range.
- Add tempo pause (1–2 s) at peak scapular retraction on rows.
- Session C: Add banded serratus wall slides (only if pain-free staying below 90°), 2 x 10.

Week 3
- Introduce 1.5-rep technique on cable rows (row, half release, row): 3 x 8.
- Incline push-up: 4 x 8–10 or reduce incline slightly.
- TRX row: increase depth slightly; 3 x 10–12.
- Landmine press or incline press: 4 x 8 if fully pain-free; else maintain.

Week 4
- Consolidate: 2 sets deload volume reduction (about 20% less total volume) while keeping quality and range.
- Reassess tolerated ROM; note any movements reproducing symptoms to avoid next phase.

Phase 2: Progress load, leverage, unilateral control (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: Build strength within allowed ROM; increase unilateral pulling/pushing; add closed-chain stability; pull:push remains ~2:1.

Week 5
Session A
- 1-arm chest-supported row: 4 x 8–10/side, moderate.
- High-incline DB bench (20–30°, neutral grip, elbows ~45°), limited ROM: 4 x 6–8.
- Landmine press (half-kneeling, ipsilateral knee down): 3 x 8/side, controlled to pain-free height.
- Sidelying ER with load progression or cable ER 0–30°: 3 x 10–12.
- Prone T (palms down) to 60–80°, light: 3 x 10–12.
- Suitcase carry heavier: 3 x 40–50 m/side.

Session B
- Seated cable row (wide neutral), 3-sec ecc: 4 x 8–10.
- Low-angle face pull to chest: 3 x 10–12.
- Push-up on rack lower setting or eccentric-only to a box (assist concentric): 4 x 6–8.
- Banded IR/ER superset at 0–30°: 2 x 15 each.
- Pallof press + overhead reach in scapular plane only to tolerance (no over-90°), 3 x 8/side.

Session C
- Chest-supported lat pulldown (neutral grip), stop at chin height without shoulder elevation: 4 x 8–10.
- TRX row feet further forward or ring row: 4 x 8–12.
- Cable low-to-mid row (rope), elbows tucked: 3 x 12.
- Biceps hammer curl + reverse curl superset: 2 x 12 each.
- Forearm pronation/supination with DB: 2 x 12 each.

Week 6
- Slight load increments; maintain 2–3 RIR.
- Add scapular depression holds on pulldown bar (active hang below 90° shoulder flexion on low bar/cables): 3 x 20 s if pain-free.
- Landmine press: add 1 set or +1–2 reps.

Week 7
- Introduce tempo clusters on rows: 2 x (6+6) with 15 s intra-set rest at same weight.
- Push-up: progress to eccentric 5 s down x 4–6 reps x 4 sets or add band-assisted full push-ups if pain-free.
- Add bottom-up KB carry (light), elbow by side: 3 x 20–30 m/side.

Week 8
- Deload: reduce total sets by ~25–30%, keep intensity moderate.
- Reassess ROM and symptom response. If entirely pain-free in all session work, consider small increases in ROM for landmine/incline patterns while still avoiding overhead.

Phase 3: Strength-endurance and climbing-specific capacity (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: Increase pulling endurance and scapular control for climbing; integrate anti-rotation, unilateral patterns, and controlled return to easy climbing drills. Maintain no overhead loading; all climbing kept sub-symptom, submax, with conservative angles.

Climbing guidance weeks 9–12
- 1–2 easy sessions/week on slab/low-angle terrain or on a systems board set to low angle with large holds.
- Rules: no dynos, no powerful lock-offs, no moves requiring arm above shoulder in painful arc, stop at first hint of impingement discomfort. Emphasize footwork, hips, and quiet scapulae. 30–45 minutes, RPE 4–5/10.

Week 9
Session A
- 1-arm cable row with 2-second isometric squeeze at end range: 4 x 8/side.
- High-incline DB bench or decline push-up (hands on parallettes, elbows 30–45°): 4 x 8.
- Landmine press to slightly increased ROM if tolerated: 4 x 6–8/side.
- Prone Y to tolerated height with very light load: 3 x 10–12.
- Bottom-up KB carry: 3 x 30–40 m/side.
Session B
- Ring/TRX row with 2–3 s eccentric: 4 x 10–12.
- Low-angle face pull + external rotation (rope split then ER), 3 x 10.
- Serratus wall slide with mini-band around forearms, stay under 90°: 3 x 8–10.
- Cable anti-rotation press with step-out: 3 x 10/side.
- Wrist extensor eccentrics + finger extensors bands: 2 x 15 each.
Session C
- Chest-supported pulldown or machine row heavy-moderate: 5 x 6–8.
- Push-up variation that is pain-free: 4 x 8–10; add band-resistance if easy and painless.
- 90/90 ER lift-off (forearm on bench, lift hand), 3 x 8–10 light.
- Biceps curl (EZ bar neutral), 3 x 10–12.
- Triceps cable (neutral/rope), elbows tucked: 2 x 12–15.

Week 10
- Progress reps or load by small amounts.
- Add controlled scapular pull-up depressions on a low bar/rings keeping shoulders below 90°: 3 x 8–10.
- Landmine press: incorporate slight pause at bottom to reinforce scapular control.

Week 11
- Strength-endurance sets:
  • TRX row EMOM: 6 minutes, 6–8 reps each minute at manageable depth.
  • Push-up EMOM: 6 minutes, 5–7 reps at current incline or floor with assistance as needed.
- Rows: one day 4 x 12–15 with 2 s squeeze.
- Add 1–2 climbing technique drills post-Session B (if not climbing same day): foot-only traverses, hip-in drills, scapular setting on big holds, 10–15 minutes.

Week 12
- Consolidation/deload: reduce sets by ~30%, maintain movement quality.
- Reassess: pain-free status, ROM, provocative positions, climbing tolerance. Plan next cycle potentially reintroducing gentle overhead in the scapular plane only with physio approval.

Optional lower-body/posture day (1–2x/week throughout)
- Goblet squat or split squat: 3 x 8–10.
- RDL or hip hinge: 3 x 8–10.
- Lateral step-downs: 2 x 10/side.
- Calf raises: 2 x 15.
- Posture: band pull-aparts (below shoulder height), thoracic extension over foam roller, 3–5 minutes.

Recovery and monitoring
- Daily micro-mobility (5–7 minutes): thoracic rotations, scapular circles, gentle pec doorway stretch (low angle), posterior cuff stretch (cross-body), all symptom-free.
- Soft-tissue: light foam rolling upper back/pec minor region as tolerated.
- Pain and load log: record any pain >3/10, night pain, or DOMS lasting >48 h at the anterior shoulder; if present, cut next session volume by 30–50% and avoid provoking exercises.
- Desk ergonomics: elbows supported, keyboard/mouse close, frequent breaks (hourly 2–3 minutes) with shoulder blade retractions.

Progression rules
- Only progress load or range if sessions and 24–48 h after are symptom-free.
- Prioritize pulling volume increases over pushing.
- Maintain neutral/hammer grips where possible.
- Keep scapulae moving: allow upward rotation and posterior tilt; avoid shrugging or anterior humeral glide.

Example week-by-week summary
- Weeks 1–2: Establish baselines; light loads; high-quality scapular and RC work.
- Week 3: Progress reps/ROM slightly; introduce 1.5-rep rows; push-ups harder variant.
- Week 4: Deload/review.
- Weeks 5–6: Moderate loads; unilateral rows and presses; improved closed-chain control.
- Week 7: Cluster/tempo progressions; begin carries challenge.
- Week 8: Deload/review.
- Weeks 9–10: Strength-endurance and climbing capacity; add scapular drills on low bars.
- Week 11: EMOM endurance emphasis; integrate short technique-focused climbing or drills.
- Week 12: Consolidate, reassess, and plan next cycle with physio input.

Notes for the trainer
- Substitute any exercise that reproduces impingement symptoms with a version using a more neutral grip, more scapular plane alignment, reduced ROM, or increased external cueing (towel under arm, elbow closer to side).
- Landmine press is a hinge between horizontal and vertical; keep arc modest and terminate before any painful pinch.
- Maintain 2:1 pulling to pushing sets each week.
- Coordinate with her physio before introducing any overhead ROM in the next block.
